name: RT-1
summary: RT-1 trained a 35M-parameter transformer on ~130k teleoperated episodes covering 700+ tasks, collected over 17 months with a fleet of 13 Everyday Robots mobile manipulators. Images pass through an EfficientNet conditioned on the instruction via FiLM, a TokenLearner compresses each frame to 8 tokens, and the transformer emits discretized arm and base actions. It ran at 3 Hz on real hardware and kept improving as data scaled rather than saturating.
innovation: Discretize continuous actions into 256 bins per dimension and predict them as tokens, turning control into next-token prediction.
TokenLearner compression made a transformer policy fast enough (3 Hz) to close the loop on real hardware.
Showed positive transfer from heterogeneous data: adding simulation and other robots' data raised real-world success instead of diluting it.
matters: Established the 'scale real robot data + one transformer' recipe every later VLA inherits.
Its 130k-episode dataset became a cornerstone of Open X-Embodiment.
limits: No web-scale pretraining, so generalization to genuinely novel objects and phrasings was weak.
Locked to one embodiment and a fixed low-frequency action space.
lineage: Applies the vanilla Transformer to robot control at fleet scale; directly extended by RT-2.
